source.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding an Attention Head
source.authors: Callum McDougall; Arthur Conmy; Cody Rushing; Thomas McGrath; Neel Nanda

page_placements.theme: Intervention conventions and metrics change evaluation conclusions
Conditional effects and query coupling reveal backups

record.tranche_reason: The study investigates copy-suppressing and backup heads in GPT-2 Small IOI, and qualifies the role of copy suppression in self-repair: it accounts for 39% in the tested setting, while backup heads use a different mechanism. It also reports copy-suppression results under different metrics and model settings.
record.gate_note: The study directly measures head effects and self-repair in IOI, and copy suppression on OpenWebText. It does not evaluate the full 26-head, seven-class IOI circuit against the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. The GPT-2 Medium and other-model results are limited to the reported QK, copy-suppression, or anti-induction analyses. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own IOI experiments in GPT-2 Small bear on three versions. It ablates the three Name Movers and decomposes the resulting self-repair (V2), and it shows the negative name-mover heads' attention is set by Name Mover output (V1, negative-head class). It also argues the negative heads do general copy suppression, reused across OpenWebText, anti-induction and other models (V3). It does not re-evaluate the full 26-head circuit, other discovery methods, or prompt variants.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Additions: the authors conclude that negative name-mover heads do general copy suppression rather than an IOI-specific algorithm, so component roles found on narrow tasks can mislead. Backup heads attend less to names that Name Movers copy (the opposite of negative heads), and neither mechanism is explained by the unembedding direction alone.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than reproducing the full IOI-circuit faithfulness, completeness, and minimality evaluation, the paper analyzes L10H7 copy suppression using logit-lens measurements, mean ablation, CSPA, weight-based QK/OV analysis, and selected IOI self-repair interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: For L10H7 on OpenWebText, reported effect recovery changes with the ablation (CSPA, OV-only, QK-only) and metric (KL divergence, net loss, absolute loss). The study also reports weaker copy-suppression instances in Pythia models.

fits_no_version.finding: CSPA's share of L10H7's effect explained varies by ablation variant and metric: KL 76.9%, OV-only 81.1%, QK-only 95.2%, net loss 82%, absolute loss 45%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How much of a single circuit component's role a mechanistic explanation captures depends on the ablation and metric chosen.

fits_no_version.finding: Backup-head self-repair in IOI is driven mainly by the part of the Name Mover output perpendicular to the IO unembedding direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The query signal that triggers backup heads is not the IO-unembedding component of Name Mover output.

record.problems: The IOI self-repair analysis is a narrow setting and addresses selected heads rather than the full circuit. Several head-level outcomes appear only in figures; no uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported results. Cross-model evidence is limited and the authors themselves note limited transferability.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported result was omitted.

untested.parts: Full 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
Backup behaviour under other ablation types, other prompt variants, or other models (except the brief Appendix Q note).
Whether full circuits with the same head classes carry IOI in other models, sizes or checkpoints; whether other circuit classes are reused for other tasks.
Not tested for the IOI circuit. The metric and ablation comparisons concern only the authors' CSPA explanation of L10H7.

missing.what: Initial look at IOI self-repair in Stanford GPT-2 Small E: a head writes 'less against' the answer after Name Mover ablation but, unlike GPT-2 Small's copy-suppression heads, attends to IO and S2 equally on clean runs.
L11H10 backs up L10H7 (self-repair between the two negative heads); controlling this path halves the indirect loss effect.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The reader's V5 links were wrong: rows r1–r5 evaluate the authors' own CSPA explanation of L10H7, not the IOI circuit, so V5 is effectively untested. The validation issue (r7, r8 under a V5 label) is resolved by relinking. V1 support is narrow: it covers only the dependency of the negative-head class on the Name Movers. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: The full 26-head, seven-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria are not evaluated. The IOI results address selected negative and backup heads, not the complete circuit.
The study examines backup behavior in the GPT-2 Small IOI setting; it does not test backup-head takeover across other prompt variants or models.

The other-model analyses do not establish that the same full circuit, head classes, and roles carry IOI across models, sizes, and checkpoints. Reuse of all circuit components for other tasks is not tested.
The study compares metrics for L10H7 copy suppression on OpenWebText, but does not systematically vary ablation methods, metrics, or prompt distributions for the full IOI circuit.

source_check.correct: state=observed for selected negative-head generalization. The two strongest QK recoveries overlap two of the three most negative IOI heads; the third head's recovery status and full-circuit identity are not established.
source_check.problem: The reported overlap does not establish incomplete recovery or a missing mechanism in the third head.
